target.name: chip-layout
target.problem: Place thousands of components on a chip so that the total wiring is as short as possible. Greedy swaps that only ever shorten the wiring get stuck in layouts that are poor but cannot be improved by any single swap.

true_source.title: Slow cooling of hot metal (annealing)
true_source.body: Smiths heat metal until it glows and then let it cool very slowly. While it is hot the atoms jostle freely and can leave awkward positions; as the temperature falls they settle into an orderly, low-energy crystal.
true_source.outcome: Slowly cooled metal is tougher and less brittle than metal cooled quickly.

distractors.title: Quenching steel in water
distractors.body: Red-hot steel is plunged into water so that it cools in seconds, locking the atoms in place.
distractors.outcome: The steel becomes very hard but brittle.

distractors.title: Ant trails to food
distractors.body: Ants lay scent trails, and shorter routes collect scent faster because ants travel them more often.
distractors.outcome: Colonies converge on short routes between nest and food.

distractors.title: Bridge truss design
distractors.body: Engineers arrange beams in triangles so that loads are carried as tension and compression.
distractors.outcome: Trusses carry heavy loads with little material.

distractors.title: Sorting a hand of cards
distractors.body: A player picks up cards one at a time and slides each into its correct place among those already held.
distractors.outcome: The hand is sorted with few moves when it is small.

truth.summary: Simulated annealing: accept some worsening swaps while a temperature-like setting is high, and lower it slowly, so the search escapes poor layouts and settles into a good one.
key_points: Occasionally accepts a move that makes the wiring longer
A temperature-like setting controls how often worse moves are accepted
The setting is lowered slowly over the course of the search

target.name: bullet-train-nose
target.problem: A high-speed train pushes a wall of air ahead of it into a tunnel, and a loud boom is heard when it leaves the far end. The shape of the nose has to change so that the pressure wave is cut.

true_source.title: Kingfisher beak diving into water
true_source.body: A kingfisher dives from air into water, two media of very different density, with hardly any splash. Its long beak widens gradually from a narrow tip into the head.
true_source.outcome: The bird enters the water cleanly and with little resistance.

distractors.title: Swallow tail for steering
distractors.body: A swallow's forked tail lets it turn sharply at speed.
distractors.outcome: Swallows catch insects in tight turns.

distractors.title: Owl feather fringes
distractors.body: Soft fringes on owl wing feathers break up turbulence so that flight is almost silent.
distractors.outcome: Owls approach prey without being heard.

distractors.title: Sound barriers beside roads
distractors.body: Tall walls beside motorways block and reflect traffic noise.

distractors.title: Rubber bumpers on carriages
distractors.body: Rubber pads between carriages absorb sudden jolts.

truth.summary: The nose was modelled on a kingfisher's beak, whose gradually widening cross-section lets air pressure build up smoothly instead of as a wall.
key_points: Nose shaped after a bird's beak that widens gradually
A gradual change in cross-section softens the air pressure wave
The result is a quieter exit from tunnels and less energy used

target.name: reusable-fastener
target.problem: A fastener is needed for clothing and gear that can be closed and opened many times without buttons, zips or ties, and that holds firmly until it is pulled apart.

true_source.title: Burdock burrs caught in dog fur
true_source.body: The seed burrs of the burdock plant are covered in tiny hooks. Under a microscope the hooks catch on the loops of fur and cloth and cling until they are pulled off.
true_source.outcome: The burrs stick firmly yet can be pulled free again and again.

distractors.title: Gecko foot hairs
distractors.body: Millions of fine hairs on a gecko's feet cling to smooth walls through molecular attraction.
distractors.outcome: Geckos climb glass walls and release their grip at will.

distractors.title: Pine cone scales
distractors.body: Pine cone scales open when dry and close when damp.
distractors.outcome: Cones release seeds on dry days.

distractors.title: Rivets in ship hulls
distractors.body: Hot metal pins are hammered through plates and flattened at both ends.
distractors.outcome: Joints are strong but cannot be undone.

distractors.title: Spider silk
distractors.body: Spiders spin strong, stretchy thread to catch prey.
distractors.outcome: Webs hold up against wind and struggling insects.

truth.summary: Velcro: one surface of tiny hooks and one of soft loops, copied from burrs and fur, so that pressing fastens and pulling releases.
key_points: A matching surface of soft loops that the hooks catch
Pressing together fastens it and pulling apart releases it repeatedly
